cards.text: When David, Israel's king, is old and full of years, he installs his son Solomon as king over Israel. Then he gathers all the leaders of Israel, plus the priests and the Levites. Big meeting, friend, the kind where NOBODY is checking their phone.
First, a head count of every Levite man thirty and older: 38,000. That is a LOT of name tags.

cards.question: David splits the 38,000 Levites into four groups. The biggest group, 24,000 men, gets which job?

answers.text: Oversee the work of the LORD's house
Keep watch at the city gates

cards.question: David's next group of Levites is 6,000 men. What does David say they are to be?
The last 8,000 Levites get split right down the middle. 4,000 become gatekeepers. What are the other 4,000 to do?

cards.text: And those instruments for giving praise are the ones David says he has made. Friend, this king didn't just join the worship team, he SUPPLIED it.

Then David divides the Levites into divisions by Levi's three sons, Gershon, Kohath and Merari, and the list runs family by family, every head of a family registered by name. One standout: Aaron, brother of Moses the man of God, and Aaron's descendants are set apart forever to consecrate the most holy things, burn incense before the LORD, minister before Him and pronounce blessings in His name.
Then comes what David had said, plain as day: "The LORD, the God of Israel, has given rest to His people and has come to dwell in Jerusalem forever."

cards.question: Since the LORD has come to dwell in Jerusalem, David says the Levites no longer need to ___ the tabernacle.

cards.text: No more hauling the tabernacle and all its articles around. I moved ONE time, from a kitchen counter to a junk drawer, and I am STILL not over it.

cards.question: Earlier, David counted the Levites thirty and older. True or false: by David's final instructions, the Levites twenty and older are counted.

cards.text: So if nobody's carrying a tent anymore, what's the job? The Levites become helpers in the service of the house of the LORD.

cards.question: The Levites are to assist with the service of the LORD's house. Who are they assisting?
The Levites are told to stay out of the courts and chambers of the LORD's house.

cards.text: Then the job list gets to the bread: the rows of the showbread, the fine flour for the grain offering and the wafers of unleavened bread. Friend, there are BAKERS in the house of the LORD, and I have never felt so seen in my life.

cards.question: The Levites also handle the baking, the mixing and all ___ of quantity and size.
On top of all that work, the Levites have a set time to stand and give thanks and praise to the LORD. When is it?

cards.text: And whenever burnt offerings are presented to the LORD on the Sabbaths, New Moons and appointed feasts, the Levites serve regularly, in the numbers set for them. Morning shift, evening shift AND holidays, friend, and that schedule does NOT come with a snooze button.

cards.question: To wrap it all up, the Levites are put in charge over the descendants of Aaron.

findings.problem: Two wrong answers describe jobs that other Levite groups really get in this passage. "Keep watch at the city gates" matches the 4,000 gatekeepers in 23:5. "Settle disputes across the land" matches the 6,000 officers and judges in 23:4. A baker could argue these are Levite duties in the passage. "Settle disputes" also points toward the answer of card 4 (officers and judges), which comes next.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Settle disputes across the land" signals the answer to the next choice card (card 4: "Officers and judges"), so the later answer is partly given away.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: "I moved ONE time, from a kitchen counter to a junk drawer" contradicts his backstory. He also moved from the closing bakery's bin to the Millers' kitchen, and from the drawer to the Dorinverse. A joke can make up small moments, but it can't change the story in papa-dorin.md.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: "Earlier, David counted the Levites thirty and older" names David as the one who counted. 1 Chronicles 23:3 is passive: "The Levites thirty years of age or older were counted." The text doesn't say who did the counting, and card 2 kept it open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "sales" doesn't fit the line ("all sales of quantity and size") and doesn't match the tone of the other answers. It reads as a throwaway, so it is easy to rule out without any reasoning.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
